newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech unions extend national rail strike - agency.
newsitem.headline: Czech unions extend national rail strike - agency.

text.p: Czech railway unions on Friday voted to extend a national rail strike, already in its fourth day, another 24 hours, the Czech news agency CTK reported, quoting the executive secretary of the unions' leadership.
Czech unions extend national rail strike =2
Mojmir Bakalar of the Association of Unions of Railway Workers (OSZ) told CTK that the strike would run through at least midnight on Saturday.

The action, which began Tuesday and was originally planned as a 48-hour work stoppage, was extended to a fourth day on Friday after both unions and the government dug in their heels, adopting hardline stances.
The OSZ are demanding removal of the Czech state railway's management and a total rethink of plans to reform the rail system which could cost tens of thousands of jobs if implemented.
Union and government officials were hopeful that the strike could be ended on Friday through a meeting of the tripartite council which combines union, industry, and government leaders.
A Prague court has ruled that the strike is illegal, but Transport Minister Martin Riman has said that striking workers would not be fired if they would return to work quickly.
